components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买; 资 is capital or resources.
次 (cì) is a loose clue; same part in 姿 zī and 咨 zī.
斗 (dipper, measure) — measuring grain and liquids: 科, 斜, 升; 料 is rice 米 measured out, then material.

example.hanzi: 我需要收集一些资料来写报告。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào shōují yìxiē zīliào lái xiě bàogào.
example.english: I need to gather some materials to write the report.
example.fact: 资料 spans a wider range than any single English word — "material" for a report, "data" for research, and in internet slang a user's personal "profile" (个人资料) — one word doing service for physical reference documents and digital identity alike.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè fèn zīliào fā gěi wǒ.
examples.english: Please send this material to me.

examples.hanzi: 图书馆里有很多学习资料。
examples.pinyin: Túshūguǎn lǐ yǒu hěn duō xuéxí zīliào.
examples.english: There are lots of study materials in the library.

components.note: 干 (dry; do) — a forked pole or shield. It lends its sound to 肝 gān, 杆 gān, 赶 gǎn, 汗 hàn and 岸 àn.
冫 (two dots) — simplified 净 uses these where traditional 淨 had 氵 water: clean by water. 争 (zhēng) is a loose sound clue; 静 jìng shares it.

example.pinyin: Bǎ fángjiān dǎsǎo gānjìng.
example.english: Clean the room thoroughly.
example.fact: 干净 frequently appears as a resultative complement tacked onto a cleaning verb — 打扫干净 ("sweep until clean"), 洗干净 ("wash until clean") — rather than standing alone; Mandarin's verb+result-adjective construction packs "do X until Y is achieved" into one compact phrase.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu xǐ de hěn gānjìng.
examples.english: This piece of clothing has been washed very clean.

examples.pinyin: Tā de fángjiān zǒngshì hěn gānjìng.
examples.english: His room is always very tidy.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
昏 (hūn, dusk) gives the exact sound; weddings were traditionally held at dusk, so the sound clue is also a meaning clue.
女 (woman) — women and family: 妈, 妹, 婚, 姑; 姻 is a bond of marriage.
因 (yīn) sounds exactly like 姻; also in 烟 yān and 恩 ēn.

example.pinyin: Tāmen de hūnyīn hěn xìngfú.
example.english: Their marriage is very happy.
example.fact: Both halves of 婚姻 are built on the 女 ("woman") radical — 婚 historically centered on the bride, and 姻 named the kinship formed through marriage — a small reminder of how the classical vocabulary around marriage was written primarily from the bride's side.

examples.hanzi: 他们的婚姻已经持续了二十年。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de hūnyīn yǐjīng chíxùle èrshí nián.
examples.english: Their marriage has lasted twenty years.

examples.hanzi: 婚姻需要双方一起努力。
examples.pinyin: Hūnyīn xūyào shuāngfāng yìqǐ nǔlì.
examples.english: Marriage requires effort from both sides.

components.note: 疒 (illness, 病字旁) — illness and pain: 病 ill, 疼 ache, 瘦 thin, 疯 mad; 痛 is pain.
甬 (yǒng) is a loose sound clue; same part in 通 tōng and 桶 tǒng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ dùzi hěn tòng.
example.english: My stomach really hurts.
example.fact: 痛 is a bit more formal than 疼 (téng) and often sharper or more emotional: 痛苦 (suffering), 痛恨 (hate bitterly), 痛哭 (weep bitterly). 痛快 ("pain-fast") oddly means happy and unrestrained.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tóutòng, xiǎng xiūxi yíxià.
examples.english: I have a headache and want to rest a while.

examples.pinyin: Tā shū le bǐsài, xīn lǐ hěn tòng.
examples.english: He lost the match and was in great pain at heart.

components.note: 亲 (qīn) keeps the sound part of the traditional 親, which also had 见; it also gives 新 xīn and 薪 xīn, so qīn/xīn is a series.

example.pinyin: Tā hé wǒ shì qīn xiōngdì.
example.english: He and I are brothers by blood.
example.fact: 亲 is closeness of blood or feeling: 父亲, 母亲, 亲戚 (relatives), 亲爱的 (dear). As a verb it is the casual "kiss" (亲一下), and Chinese online sellers address customers as 亲, like "dear".

examples.hanzi: 这是我的亲戚，他是我舅舅。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de qīnqi, tā shì wǒ jiùjiu.
examples.english: This is my relative; he is my uncle.

examples.pinyin: Māma qīn le wǒ yíxià.
examples.english: Mom kissed me.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions applied to people: 放, 改, 政; 教 is to teach, traditionally with a rod.
孝 (xiào) is a near sound match for jiào; also in 酵 jiào.
土 (earth) — ground and building sites: 地, 场, 块; 堂 is a raised hall.
尚 (shàng) gives the -ang sound; same part in 常 cháng, 掌 zhǎng, 堂 táng.

example.hanzi: 他们在教堂举行了婚礼。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài jiàotáng jǔxíngle hūnlǐ.
example.english: They held their wedding at the church.
example.fact: 教堂 literally means "a hall (堂) for religion/teaching (教)" — the same 教 that gives 教育 ("education") and 宗教 ("religion") is paired here with 堂, the generic word for a large ceremonial hall also seen in 食堂 ("dining hall") and 礼堂 ("auditorium").

examples.hanzi: 这座教堂有一百年的历史。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò jiàotáng yǒu yì bǎi nián de lìshǐ.
examples.english: This church has a hundred years of history.

examples.hanzi: 周日早上，很多人去教堂。
examples.pinyin: Zhōurì zǎoshang, hěn duō rén qù jiàotáng.
examples.english: On Sunday mornings, many people go to church.

components.note: 皮 (skin) — a hand 又 stripping hide from an animal; 皮 also sounds out 披 pī, 坡 pō and 玻 bō.

example.pinyin: Zhège píngguǒ de pí hěn báo.
example.english: This apple's skin is very thin.
example.fact: 皮 covers skin, peel and leather: 皮肤 (skin), 皮鞋 (leather shoes), 苹果皮 (apple peel). Used as an adjective it also means naughty: 这孩子很皮, "that kid is mischievous".

examples.hanzi: 我吃橘子的时候要先剥皮。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chī júzi de shíhou yào xiān bāo pí.
examples.english: When I eat tangerines, I peel them first.

examples.pinyin: Zhège píbāo shì zhēnpí de.
examples.english: This leather bag is real leather.

components.note: 鸟 — the picture of a bird; simplified from 鳥. The bird radical, as in 鸡 chicken, 鸭 duck, 鸽 pigeon.

example.pinyin: Shù shang yǒu yì zhī niǎo.
example.english: There is a bird in the tree.
example.fact: 鸟 counts with 只 (一只鸟) and is the radical in many bird names, such as 鸡 and 鸭. The slang reading diǎo is crude, so learners should stick to niǎo for the animal.

examples.pinyin: Niǎo zài shù shang chànggē.
examples.english: The birds are singing in the tree.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎoniǎo fēi huí le zìjǐ de jiā.
examples.english: The little bird flew back to its nest.

components.note: 大 (big) with four 爻 marks — an open, airy feel; 爽 is crisp, refreshing and frank, as in 凉爽 cool and refreshing.

example.pinyin: Xǐ wán zǎo, gǎnjué zhēn shuǎng.
example.english: I feel so refreshed after the bath.
example.fact: 爽 means refreshing or satisfying, as in 凉爽 (cool and crisp) and the slang 爽! for "that feels great". It also means straightforward (爽快) and, surprisingly, to break a promise: 爽约 means to stand someone up.

examples.hanzi: 今天的天气真爽，不冷也不热。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de tiānqì zhēn shuǎng, bù lěng yě bú rè.
examples.english: The weather today is really refreshing, neither cold nor hot.

examples.pinyin: Tā huídá de hěn shuǎngkuài.
examples.english: He answered promptly and openly.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 健 is a strong body.
建 (jiàn) sounds exactly like 健; also in 键 jiàn.
广 (house) — the top-left cover, as in 店 shop and 床 bed; it marks a building or room.
隶 (servant) — inside 广. Dictionary story: a home with a servant, healthy and untroubled, hence 健康 health; origin is uncertain, so memory aid only.

example.pinyin: Duō yùndòng duì jiànkāng yǒu hǎochù.
example.english: Exercising more is good for health.
example.fact: 健康 works as both noun ("health," 关心健康, "care about one's health") and adjective ("healthy," 他很健康, "he is healthy") without changing form — one more case in this deck where a single Chinese word covers what English splits into two.

examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēntǐ jiànkāng!
examples.english: Wishing you good health!

examples.hanzi: 我爷爷很健康，每天都散步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye hěn jiànkāng, měi tiān dōu sànbù.
examples.english: My grandfather is very healthy and walks every day.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; a guest is a person under your roof.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 路 lù, 洛 luò, 落 luò.
户 (door, household) — one half of a double door 門. As a radical it marks doors and rooms: 房 room, 所 place, 扇 fan.

example.hanzi: 这家公司有很多国外客户。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī yǒu hěnduō guówài kèhù.
example.english: This company has many overseas clients.
example.fact: 客户 is the business-register word for a paying client or account holder — a bank, a law firm, a software company all have 客户 — while a shopper walking into a physical store is more often called 顾客; 客户 leans professional/B2B, 顾客 leans retail/everyday.

examples.hanzi: 我们要把客户放在第一位。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎ kèhù fàng zài dì yī wèi.
examples.english: We must put customers first.

examples.hanzi: 这位客户想和你谈谈价格。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi kèhù xiǎng hé nǐ tántan jiàgé.
examples.english: This client wants to talk to you about the price.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — a ring that encloses; also in 国 country, 围 surround.
卷 (juǎn) gives a close sound; 圈 also reads juàn or juān.

example.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèngquè dá'àn shang huà quān.
example.english: Please circle the correct answer.
example.fact: 圈 is a circle or ring and counts laps: 跑一圈 (run one lap). It also means social circle, which is why WeChat Moments is called 朋友圈, "circle of friends".

examples.pinyin: Háizimen wéi chéng le yí gè quān.
examples.english: The children formed a circle.

examples.hanzi: 他每天绕着操场跑三圈。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān rào zhe cāochǎng pǎo sān quān.
examples.english: Every day he runs three laps around the sports field.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 肚 belly, 脚 foot, 脸 face, 胖 fat; 脑 is the brain.
The right half shows hair over a skull and also sounds out 恼 nǎo and 瑙 nǎo.
衣 (clothing, cloth) — clothes and cloth: 装, 被, 衬; 袋 is a bag made of cloth.
代 (dài) sounds exactly like 袋; also in 贷 dài.

example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn zhuàngdàole nǎodai.
example.english: He accidentally bumped his head.
example.fact: 脑袋 is the casual, colloquial word for "head" — the plainer, more neutral term is simply 头, usable everywhere — much like English has both plain "head" and the more informal "noggin," with 脑袋 pitched at that friendlier, chattier register.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān nǎodai hěn téng.
examples.english: My head hurts a lot today.

examples.hanzi: 你的小脑袋里都在想什么？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de xiǎo nǎodai lǐ dōu zài xiǎng shénme?
examples.english: What is going on in that little head of yours?

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
句 (jù, sentence) is a close sound clue for gòu; also in 构 gòu, 沟 gōu and 钩 gōu.
多 (many) — meaning "more than enough".

example.pinyin: Zhèxiē qián búgòu mǎi jīpiào.
example.english: This money isn't enough to buy a plane ticket.
example.fact: 不够 can modify a noun directly (钱不够, "[the] money [is] not enough") or an adjective to mean "not X enough" (不够好, "not good enough") — the same negated 够 covers both a quantity shortfall and a quality shortfall, two ideas English keeps grammatically apart.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shíjiān bú gòu le.
examples.english: I don't have enough time.

examples.pinyin: Tā de nǔlì hái bú gòu.
examples.english: His effort is still not enough.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 嘘 is exhaling or hushing.
虚 (xū) — same sound: 嘘 xū. 虚 also sounds out 墟 xū.

example.pinyin: Xū, xiǎoshēng diǎn, bǎobao shuì zháo le.
example.english: Shh, be quiet, the baby is asleep.
example.fact: 嘘 is the "shh!" sound for hushing, and it also means to hiss or boo (嘘声). The idiom 嘘寒问暖 ("puff warmth, ask about the cold") describes caring attentively for someone's well-being.

examples.pinyin: Xū, bié shuōhuà, lǎoshī lái le.
examples.english: Shh, don't talk; the teacher is coming.

examples.hanzi: 他嘘了一口气，终于放松了。
examples.pinyin: Tā xū le yì kǒu qì, zhōngyú fàngsōng le.
examples.english: He let out a breath and finally relaxed.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.pinyin: Qiánmiàn yǒu yígè hónglǜdēng.
example.english: There's a traffic light ahead.
example.fact: 前面 pairs with 后面 ("behind") the way 上面/下面 pair for "above/below" — 面 ("face, surface, side") is Mandarin's default suffix for turning a bare directional word into a locatable place, the building block behind a whole family: 前面, 后面, 里面, 外面.

examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn jiùshì wǒ jiā.
examples.english: My home is just ahead.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zhàn zài duìwu de qiánmiàn.
examples.english: Please stand at the front of the line.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.pinyin: Tāmen shàng gè yuè fēnshǒu le.
example.english: They broke up last month.
example.fact: 分手 literally means "to divide (分) hands (手)" — unclasping joined hands as a physical image for parting ways, whether between traveling companions heading off in different directions or, in its most common modern use, a couple ending a relationship.

examples.hanzi: 他们决定分手，但仍然是朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen juédìng fēnshǒu, dàn réngrán shì péngyou.
examples.english: They decided to break up but are still friends.

examples.hanzi: 她为了工作和男朋友分手了。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèile gōngzuò hé nánpéngyou fēnshǒu le.
examples.english: She broke up with her boyfriend because of work.

components.note: 方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.
向 (toward) — a window 口 in a wall facing a direction, hence toward. It also gives its sound to 响 xiǎng and 饷 xiǎng.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zǒucuò fāngxiàng le.
example.english: We went the wrong direction.
example.fact: 方向 moves easily from the literal — which way to walk or drive, 问方向 ("ask for directions") — to the figurative, as in a life or career's general direction (人生方向) — much like English "direction" itself bridges the physical and the metaphorical without needing a separate word for either.

examples.hanzi: 这个方向是去火车站的吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge fāngxiàng shì qù huǒchēzhàn de ma?
examples.english: Is this the direction to the train station?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào zhǎodào zìjǐ de fāngxiàng.
examples.english: You need to find your own direction.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.pinyin: Tā qù kàn xīnlǐ yīshēng le.
example.english: He went to see a psychologist.
example.fact: 心理 (xīnlǐ, "psychology/mentality") is easy to mix up with the near-homophone 心里 (xīnli, "inside one's heart, in one's thoughts") — swapping 理 ("reason, logic") for 里 ("inside") turns a clinical or academic noun into an everyday phrase for private feelings, a mix-up that shows up even in native speakers' typos.

examples.pinyin: Tā de xīnlǐ yālì hěn dà.
examples.english: He is under great psychological pressure.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì xīnlǐxué hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.english: I'm very interested in psychology.

components.note: 幸 (luck) — often read as an old picture of shackles; 'luck' is escaping punishment. The dictionary story (one alive 土, one dead 干) is a memory aid.
土 (earth) — the top. Memory aid: the one standing on solid ground 土 is the lucky one — 幸运, 幸福.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and blessings: 神, 礼, 祝, 祈; 福 is good fortune from the gods.
畐 (fú) sounds exactly like 福; also in 幅 fú, 副 fù, 富 fù.

example.pinyin: Zhù nǐmen xìngfú měimǎn.
example.english: Wishing you happiness and fulfillment.
example.fact: 幸福 describes a deep, lasting sense of well-being and contentment — often tied to family, marriage, or life circumstances — setting it apart from the lighter, more momentary 高兴 or 开心 ("happy, glad" in the moment); saying 祝你幸福 at a wedding carries far more weight than a casual 祝你开心.

examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēnghuó xìngfú!
examples.english: Wishing you a happy life!

examples.hanzi: 一家人在一起就是幸福。
examples.pinyin: Yì jiā rén zài yìqǐ jiùshì xìngfú.
examples.english: Being together as a family is happiness.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wood, as in 林, 桥, 板; 树 is a tree.
对 (duì) is a stand-in for an older sound part 尌 (shù), not a sound clue itself.

example.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ yǒu yì kē dà shù.
example.english: There's a big tree in the yard.
example.fact: 树 counts with 棵 (一棵树). As a verb it means to establish: 树立. The proverb 十年树木，百年树人 (ten years to grow a tree, a hundred to cultivate people) is the classic line about education.

examples.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ zhòng le hěn duō shù.
examples.english: Many trees are planted in the park.

examples.hanzi: 他为公司树立了好形象。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèi gōngsī shùlì le hǎo xíngxiàng.
examples.english: He established a good image for the company.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions taken on something: 教, 放, 改; 救 is to take action to rescue.
求 (qiú) is a near sound match for jiù; 求 also means ask for help.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: an order is spoken.
令 (lìng, order) is a close sound clue for mìng; 令 also in 领 lǐng, 冷 lěng and 零 líng.

example.pinyin: “Jiùmìng!” tā dàshēng hǎndào.
example.english: "Help!" she shouted loudly.
example.fact: As a stand-alone interjection, 救命! functions like English "Help!" in an emergency, but unlike "help," which can request any kind of assistance, 救命 literally invokes life-or-death stakes ("save my life") — so it's reserved for genuine danger rather than an everyday request for a hand.

examples.hanzi: 有人掉到水里了，快救命！
examples.pinyin: Yǒu rén diào dào shuǐ lǐ le, kuài jiùmìng!
examples.english: Someone fell into the water, help quick!

examples.hanzi: 这位医生救过很多人的命，真是救命恩人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yīshēng jiùguo hěn duō rén de mìng, zhēn shì jiùmìng ēnrén.
examples.english: This doctor has saved many lives, truly a lifesaver.

meanings: to go on to do sth

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.
著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.

example.hanzi: 先吃饭,接着我们去看电影。
example.pinyin: Xiān chīfàn, jiēzhe wǒmen qù kàn diànyǐng.
example.english: First let's eat, then we'll go watch a movie.
example.fact: As a connective opening a new clause, 接着 sequences events one after another ("and then, next") — distinct from the literal verb sense of 接 alone, "to catch" (接球, "catch a ball"), where here 着 works as a grammatical suffix rather than contributing a separate meaning of its own.

examples.hanzi: 他先洗手，接着开始做饭。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiān xǐshǒu, jiēzhe kāishǐ zuòfàn.
examples.english: He washed his hands first, then started to cook.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān shuō, wǒ jiēzhe shuō.
examples.english: You speak first, and I'll go on after you.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — heads and faces: 头, 额 forehead, 题 title, 领 collar; 项 first meant the neck.
工 (gōng) is only a loose sound hint for xiàng.

example.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù yǒu sān xiàng rènwu.
example.english: This project has three tasks.
example.fact: 项 is a measure word for items, tasks and events: 一项任务, 一项比赛. It builds 项目 (project) and 项链 (necklace, literally "neck chain"), keeping its original sense of neck.

examples.hanzi: 他是个很有爱心的人，每项工作都做得很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè hěn yǒu àixīn de rén, měi xiàng gōngzuò dōu zuò de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He is a caring person and does every task well.

examples.hanzi: 这项比赛一共有十个人参加。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng bǐsài yígòng yǒu shí gè rén cānjiā.
examples.english: Ten people are taking part in this competition.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — illness, as in 病 sick, 痛 pain, 疼 ache: madness is an illness.
风 (fēng, wind) gives the exact sound; also in 枫 fēng.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.pinyin: Bié lǐ tā, tā shì gè fēngzi.
example.english: Don't pay attention to him, he's a lunatic.
example.fact: 疯子 is a blunt, often insulting way to call someone "crazy" — for a softer or more clinical way to talk about mental illness, Chinese instead reaches for 精神病 (a mental disorder) or the plain adjective 疯 alone (他疯了, "he's gone crazy"), which describes a temporary state rather than labeling the person.

examples.hanzi: 他有时候像个疯子一样大笑。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu shíhou xiàng ge fēngzi yíyàng dà xiào.
examples.english: Sometimes he laughs wildly like a madman.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的疯子科学家做了一个怪机器。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de fēngzi kēxuéjiā zuòle yí ge guài jīqì.
examples.english: The mad scientist in the movie built a strange machine.

components.note: 贝 (cowrie) — money and value, as in 财, 货, 买: competing for prizes was once tied to offerings and stakes.

example.pinyin: Míngtiān yǒu yì chǎng zúqiú sài.
example.english: There is a football match tomorrow.
example.fact: 赛 is a contest, counted with 场: 一场比赛. It forms 比赛 (match), 决赛 (final), 赛跑 (race) and 赛车 (racing car). Note that it is a bound word rather than a free noun.

examples.hanzi: 我们队赢了今天的比赛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen duì yíng le jīntiān de bǐsài.
examples.english: Our team won today's match.

examples.pinyin: Gēge hé dìdi zài sàipǎo.
examples.english: My older brother and younger brother are racing.

meanings: to put sb on the spot

components.note: 丬 (bed/couch, left side) — the left strip, a bed seen sideways. Dictionary story: going to bed at night, the 'future' that is sure to come; read as a memory aid.
夕 (evening) — upper part of the right side, as in 外 and 多; with 寸 (hand/inch) it frames 将 meaning 'about to / will'.
车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.

example.hanzi: 这位将军带领军队赢得了战争。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi jiāngjūn dàilǐng jūnduì yíngdéle zhànzhēng.
example.english: This general led the army to win the war.
example.fact: Beyond the literal military rank, 将军 doubles as the Chinese-chess (xiangqi) term for "check" — calling out 将军! when directly threatening the opponent's general piece — and by extension the phrase is used figuratively outside the game to mean cornering someone or putting them on the spot, similar to how English "checkmate" became a metaphor beyond the chessboard.

examples.pinyin: Jiāngjūn zài dìtú qián sīkǎo.
examples.english: The general is thinking in front of the map.

examples.hanzi: 他是一位受人尊敬的将军。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi shòu rén zūnjìng de jiāngjūn.
examples.english: He is a respected general.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 技 is hand skill.
支 (zhī) is a loose sound clue; same part in 枝 zhī and 肢 zhī.
術 (traditional) — 行 (road) plus 朮 (zhú) as sound: art, method. 术 is the sound part alone; same sound in 述 shù, as in 手术, 技术, 艺术.

example.hanzi: 这家公司在人工智能技术方面很领先。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zài réngōng zhìnéng jìshù fāngmiàn hěn lǐngxiān.
example.english: This company is a leader in AI technology.
example.fact: 术 alone broadly means "art, skill, technique" and shows up across many domains — 艺术 ("art"), 手术 ("surgery," literally "hand technique"), 武术 ("martial arts") — with 技术 narrowing that general root specifically toward technical or engineering know-how.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge yīshēng de jìshù hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This doctor's skill is excellent.

examples.pinyin: Xīn jìshù ràng shēnghuó gèng fāngbiàn.
examples.english: New technology makes life more convenient.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — eating and speech: 喝, 吸, 吗; 吃 is to eat.
乞 (qǐ) is only a loose sound clue for chī.
饣 (food, simplified 食) — meals and eating: 饿 hungry, 饱 full, 饺 dumpling; 饭 is cooked rice or a meal.
反 (fǎn) is a near sound match for fàn; also in 板 bǎn.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen jǐdiǎn chīfàn?
example.english: What time are we eating?
example.fact: 吃饭 literally means "to eat rice," yet it's used nationwide as the generic "to eat a meal" even in northern China, where wheat noodles and bread are the actual staple — a case where a word's literal ingredient outlived its literal accuracy. It also extends idiomatically to "make a living" (靠什么吃饭, literally "what do you rely on to eat rice").

examples.pinyin: Nǐ chīfàn le ma?
examples.english: Have you eaten yet?

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiān chīfàn, ránhòu zài liáo.
examples.english: Let's eat first and then chat.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.

example.hanzi: 请把这个消息传给大家。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhège xiāoxi chuán gěi dàjiā.
example.english: Please pass this news on to everyone.
example.fact: 传 is to pass on, as in 传染 (infect), 传说 (legend) and 传统 (tradition). Read zhuàn, the same character means a biography (自传, 传记): a classic two-reading trap.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè fēng xìn chuángěi tā.
examples.english: Please pass this letter on to him.

examples.hanzi: 这个好消息很快就传开了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège hǎo xiāoxi hěn kuài jiù chuánkāi le.
examples.english: This good news spread quickly.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree 木 boxed in by an enclosure 囗: trapped, hemmed in; hence 困难 difficulty.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.

example.pinyin: Kèfú kùnnan xūyào yǒngqì.
example.english: Overcoming difficulties requires courage.
example.fact: 困难 functions as both adjective ("difficult," 这很困难) and noun ("a difficulty/hardship," 遇到困难, "encounter difficulties") — and unlike many two-character adjectives, it can be directly counted with 个 (一个困难, "one difficulty") once used as a noun, treating an abstract hardship almost like a countable object.

examples.pinyin: Zhè dào tí hěn kùnnan.
examples.english: This problem is very difficult.

examples.pinyin: Tā jiā de jīngjì yǒuxiē kùnnan.
examples.english: His family is in somewhat difficult financial circumstances.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: giving permission is spoken.
午 (wǔ) is only a loose sound clue for xǔ.

example.hanzi: 妈妈不许我看电视到很晚。
example.pinyin: Māma bùxǔ wǒ kàn diànshì dào hěn wǎn.
example.english: Mom doesn't allow me to watch TV until very late.
example.fact: 不许 carries a sharper, more authoritative edge than the neutral 不能 ("cannot, may not") — it's the word a parent, teacher, or rule invokes to flatly forbid something (不许说话! "No talking!"), closer in force to a command than to a simple statement of impossibility.

examples.pinyin: Shàngkè shí bù xǔ shuōhuà.
examples.english: No talking during class.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸不许我一个人去游泳。
examples.pinyin: Bàba bù xǔ wǒ yí ge rén qù yóuyǒng.
examples.english: Dad doesn't allow me to go swimming alone.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 某 first named a sour tree fruit; now it means a certain, unnamed one. It sounds out 媒 méi, 煤 méi and 谋 móu.
禾 (grain) — crops, as in 秋 autumn, 租 rent, 和 and 秒 second; 种 is seed or to plant.
中 (zhōng) is a close sound clue for zhǒng/zhòng.

example.hanzi: 他这样做一定有某种原因。
example.pinyin: Tā zhèyàng zuò yídìng yǒu mǒuzhǒng yuányīn.
example.english: He must have some kind of reason for doing this.
example.fact: 某 alone means “a certain, some (unspecified)” and can even be doubled to 某某 for extra vagueness — like English “so-and-so” — while 某种 keeps that same vagueness but locks it onto a category with 种 (“kind, type”), a common hedging device for softening a claim without naming specifics.

examples.hanzi: 这件事我们某种程度上都有责任。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒmen mǒu zhǒng chéngdù shàng dōu yǒu zérèn.
examples.english: To some extent we are all responsible for this.

examples.pinyin: Tā hǎoxiàng déle mǒu zhǒng bìng.
examples.english: He seems to have some kind of illness.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 忆 is remembering in the heart.
乙 (yǐ) stands in for 意 (yì) in the old form 憶, so it is a close sound clue for yì.

example.hanzi: 他还保留着童年的记忆。
example.pinyin: Tā hái bǎoliú zhe tóngnián de jìyì.
example.english: He still holds onto memories from his childhood.
example.fact: In everyday speech “to remember” is almost always 记得 (jìde), not 记忆 — 记忆 functions mainly as the noun “memory,” so using it to mean “I remember...” reads as unusually formal or literary to a native speaker, a common trap for learners translating “memory” and “remember” too literally from their shared English root.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌是我美好的记忆。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē shì wǒ měihǎo de jìyì.
examples.english: This song is a fond memory of mine.

examples.hanzi: 我的记忆力不好，常常忘事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jìyìlì bù hǎo, chángcháng wàngshì.
examples.english: My memory isn't good and I often forget things.

components.note: 乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.

example.hanzi: 这个乐队上个月发了新专辑。
example.pinyin: Zhège yuèduì shàng gè yuè fā le xīn zhuānjí.
example.english: This band released a new album last month.
example.fact: 乐 is one of Mandarin's most notorious multi-reading characters: lè (“happy,” as in 快乐) versus yuè (“music,” as in 音乐) — the two readings share no tone relationship at all, and 乐队 always takes the yuè reading since it names a “music team,” never a “happy” one.

examples.hanzi: 这个乐队的主唱声音很好听。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge yuèduì de zhǔchàng shēngyīn hěn hǎotīng.
examples.english: This band's lead singer has a lovely voice.

examples.hanzi: 我弟弟想加入学校的乐队。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi xiǎng jiārù xuéxiào de yuèduì.
examples.english: My younger brother wants to join the school band.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 经, 系: a pulled-tight cord. The top part is also in 坚 jiān (firm).
心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 急 is a heart in a hurry. The top is a variant of 及 (jí, reach), the same sound as in 级 and 极.

example.hanzi: 遇到紧急情况,请拨打这个电话。
example.pinyin: Yùdào jǐnjí qíngkuàng, qǐng bōdǎ zhège diànhuà.
example.english: In case of an emergency, please call this number.
example.fact: 紧急 almost always modifies a fixed set of nouns rather than standing alone — 紧急情况 (“emergency situation”), 紧急会议 (“emergency meeting”), 紧急出口 (“emergency exit”) — learning it inside these set phrases sticks better than memorizing the adjective by itself.

examples.hanzi: 这件事很紧急，请马上处理。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì hěn jǐnjí, qǐng mǎshàng chǔlǐ.
examples.english: This matter is urgent, please handle it right away.

examples.hanzi: 医院每天都有紧急的病人。
examples.pinyin: Yīyuàn měi tiān dōu yǒu jǐnjí de bìngrén.
examples.english: The hospital has emergency patients every day.

components.note: 高 (tall) — a drawing of a tall tower building. 高 also sounds out 糕 gāo (cake), 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 我妹妹现在读高中二年级。
example.pinyin: Wǒ mèimei xiànzài dú gāozhōng èr niánjí.
example.english: My little sister is now in the second year of high school.
example.fact: 高中 is short for 高级中学 (“senior/advanced middle school”), sitting above 初中 (junior high, short for 初级中学) in China's three-tier 小学–初中–高中 (elementary–junior–senior) school system — a structure English's single word “high school” doesn't name a junior tier for at all.

examples.pinyin: Tā míngnián yào shàng gāozhōng le.
examples.english: He will start senior high school next year.

examples.hanzi: 我们高中同学每年都聚一次。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gāozhōng tóngxué měi nián dōu jù yí cì.
examples.english: My high school classmates get together once every year.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.
口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.

example.hanzi: 你听听这首歌,好不好听?
example.pinyin: Nǐ tīngting zhè shǒu gē, hǎo bù hǎotīng?
example.english: Listen to this song for a sec — does it sound good?
example.fact: Doubling a one-syllable verb like 听→听听 is a common softening device in spoken Mandarin, turning a plain command into a casual, low-commitment suggestion (“just take a listen”) — the same pattern behind 看看 (“take a quick look”) and 试试 (“give it a try”), with the second syllable typically toned down to neutral in speech.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān tīngting dàjiā de yìjiàn.
examples.english: First listen to everyone's opinions.

examples.hanzi: 你听听，外面是不是下雨了？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ tīngting, wàimiàn shì bu shì xià yǔ le?
examples.english: Listen, is it raining outside?

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 我正好有时间,可以帮你。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhènghǎo yǒu shíjiān, kěyǐ bāng nǐ.
example.english: I happen to have time right now, I can help you.
example.fact: 正好 sits at the intersection of “precisely” (正, as in 正在) and “good, fitting” (好) — it can describe a lucky coincidence in timing (你来得正好, “you came at just the right moment”) or an exact fit in size or amount, covering ground that English splits across “just in time,” “just right,” and “as it happens.”

examples.hanzi: 你来得正好，我们正要吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lái de zhènghǎo, wǒmen zhèng yào chīfàn.
examples.english: You came just in time, we're about to eat.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié de dàxiǎo zhènghǎo.
examples.english: The size of these shoes is just right.

components.note: 州 (region) — a river 川 with small islands of land in it; 州 is a region, and also sounds out 洲 zhōu.

example.pinyin: Wǒ qù guo Guǎngzhōu.
example.english: I have been to Guangzhou.
example.fact: 州 was an ancient administrative division and survives in city names (广州, 杭州, 苏州) and in the names of U.S. states (加州 California). The meaning "islet" was later split into its own character 洲, which now means continent (亚洲).

examples.pinyin: Tā zài Guǎngzhōu gōngzuò le wǔ nián.
examples.english: He worked in Guangzhou for five years.

examples.hanzi: 杭州是一个很美的城市，苏州也不错。
examples.pinyin: Hángzhōu shì yí gè hěn měi de chéngshì, Sūzhōu yě búcuò.
examples.english: Hangzhou is a beautiful city, and Suzhou is nice too.

components.note: 毛 (hair, fur) — hair and fine things: 毯 blanket, 尾 tail; 毫 is fine hair, then a tiny amount, as in 毫米 millimeter.
高 (gāo) is only a loose sound hint for háo.
無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.

example.pinyin: Tā duì zhè jiàn shì háowú xìngqù.
example.english: He has absolutely no interest in this matter.
example.fact: 毫 originally meant a fine hair (as in 毫米, “millimeter,” literally a “hair-meter”) — 毫无 borrows that image of the smallest possible sliver to intensify a negation, literally “not even a hair's worth,” the same rhetorical move behind English “not one iota.”

examples.pinyin: Tā háowú bànfǎ, zhǐhǎo děngzhe.
examples.english: He had no way out and could only wait.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiǎngfǎ háowú yìyì.
examples.english: This idea is completely meaningless.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks: 酒, 醉 drunk, 酸 sour; 醒 is sobering up, then waking.
星 (xīng) sounds exactly like 醒 (tone differs).

example.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ tíxǐng wǒ.
example.english: Thank you for reminding me.
example.fact: 提醒 literally combines “to lift, raise” (提) with “to wake up” (醒) — reminding someone is pictured as “raising them out of sleep,” a vivid compositional image underlying a fairly abstract, everyday verb.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng tíxǐng wǒ míngtiān kāihuì.
examples.english: Please remind me of tomorrow's meeting.

examples.pinyin: Yīshēng tíxǐng tā yào shǎo chī yán.
examples.english: The doctor reminded him to eat less salt.

components.note: 旅 (travel) — a flag with people gathered under it: a troop on the march, then travellers on a journey.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.hanzi: 我们计划暑假去欧洲旅行。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen jìhuà shǔjià qù Ōuzhōu lǚxíng.
example.english: We're planning to travel to Europe during summer vacation.
example.fact: 旅 is pronounced lǚ with the “ü” vowel — one of a small set of Mandarin syllables (旅, 女, 绿, 吕) that keep the umlaut in pinyin because dropping it (writing plain “lu”) would collide with an entirely different syllable already claimed by “lu” (as in 路, 六); the umlaut is a genuine, load-bearing part of the spelling, not a decorative accent.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan yí ge rén lǚxíng.
examples.english: I like traveling alone.

examples.hanzi: 这次旅行我们玩得很开心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng wǒmen wán de hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: We had a great time on this trip.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 惊 is a startled heart.
京 (jīng) sounds exactly like 惊; also in 鲸 jīng and 景 jǐng.
壴 (zhù, drum) — a drum on top of 口 mouth: music and singing, joy.
口 (mouth) — singing and speaking, as in 唱 sing, 吃 eat.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhēnshi yí gè jīngxǐ!
example.english: This is such a nice surprise!
example.fact: 惊喜 fuses “shock, fright” (惊, as in 惊讶) with “joy” (喜, as in 喜欢) into a single word for specifically the pleasant flavor of surprise — Chinese keeps this distinct from a bad shock, which instead pairs 惊 with 吓 (惊吓, “to be frightened”), splitting “surprise” along a good/bad axis that English's one word doesn't mark.

examples.hanzi: 朋友们给我准备了一个惊喜。
examples.pinyin: Péngyoumen gěi wǒ zhǔnbèile yí ge jīngxǐ.
examples.english: My friends prepared a surprise for me.

examples.hanzi: 看到她突然回来，我又惊喜又感动。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào tā tūrán huílái, wǒ yòu jīngxǐ yòu gǎndòng.
examples.english: Seeing her suddenly return, I was pleasantly surprised and moved.

components.note: 手 (hand) — the bottom form shows a hand; 拿 is two hands closing 合 on something: to take hold.
走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ nǐ de dōngxi názǒu.
example.english: Please take your things away.
example.fact: 走 tacked onto a verb as a directional complement marks the object moving away from the scene — 拿走 (“take away”) and 带走 (“take/bring along away”) both point outward, while swapping in 来 or 去 instead of 走 would point the same action toward a destination — a small but productive family of verb-plus-direction pairs.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ názǒu zhuō shàng de shū.
examples.english: You can take the books off the table.

examples.hanzi: 别人没有把我的伞拿走吧？
examples.pinyin: Biéren méiyǒu bǎ wǒ de sǎn názǒu ba?
examples.english: Surely no one has taken my umbrella?

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 远, 送: coming closer.
斤 (jīn) is a close sound clue for jìn.

example.hanzi: 他的年龄接近三十岁了。
example.pinyin: Tā de niánlíng jiējìn sānshí suì le.
example.english: He is getting close to thirty years old.
example.fact: 接近 works equally for physical distance (接近终点, “nearing the finish line”) and abstract closeness in age, degree, or time (接近三十岁, “nearing thirty”) — a flexibility English's “approaching” mirrors, while its near-synonym 靠近 is used mainly for the physical sense.

examples.hanzi: 春节接近了，街上很热闹。
examples.pinyin: Chūnjié jiējìn le, jiē shang hěn rènao.
examples.english: The Spring Festival is approaching and the streets are lively.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen de xiǎngfǎ hěn jiējìn.
examples.english: Their ideas are very close.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 逮 is to chase and catch. 隶 shows a hand grabbing a tail.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 捕 is to seize.
甫 (fǔ) is a loose clue; also in 铺 pù, 辅 fǔ, 薄 báo.

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了三名嫌疑人。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dàibǔ le sān míng xiányírén.
example.english: The police arrested three suspects.
example.fact: 逮 carries two different readings depending on register — the colloquial dǎi (“to catch, nab,” as in 猫逮老鼠, “the cat catches mice”) versus the formal, legal dài used only in 逮捕 (“to arrest”) — the same character splits into an everyday reading and a bureaucratic one, and mixing them up is an easy slip for learners.

examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá dàibǔle nà ge xiǎotōu.
examples.english: The police arrested the thief.

examples.hanzi: 他因为偷东西被逮捕了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi tōu dōngxi bèi dàibǔ le.
examples.english: He was arrested for stealing.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 吵 is noisy speech.
少 (shǎo) — near sound — 吵 is chǎo; 少 also sounds out 炒 chǎo and 抄 chāo.

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn tài chǎo le, wǒ shuì bù zháo.
example.english: It's too noisy outside, I can't sleep.
example.fact: 吵 is noisy as an adjective and to quarrel as a verb: 吵架 (argue). 吵醒 means to wake someone with noise, and 别吵 means "don't make noise". It is milder than 闹 (nào), which suggests more commotion.

examples.pinyin: Línjū tài chǎo le, wǒ shuìbuzháo.
examples.english: The neighbors are too loud for me to sleep.

examples.pinyin: Bié chǎo le, wǒmen hǎohāo shuō.
examples.english: Stop arguing; let's talk it over properly.

components.note: 方 (fāng) is a near sound match for páng (-ang); 方 also sounds out 房 fáng and 防 fáng.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.

example.pinyin: Yínháng jiù zài chāoshì pángbiān.
example.english: The bank is right next to the supermarket.
example.fact: 旁边 is one of Mandarin's location nouns: it attaches directly after the noun it modifies (超市旁边, “next to the supermarket”) and then combines with 在 to form a place phrase — unlike English “next to,” which acts as a preposition, 旁边 grammatically behaves as a noun meaning “the side/vicinity,” a structural quirk it shares with 里面 (“inside”) and 上面 (“on top”).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā pángbiān yǒu yì jiā chāoshì.
examples.english: There is a supermarket next to my home.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ zuò zài wǒ pángbiān.
examples.english: Please sit beside me.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 激 is water surging up, then to stir up.
敫 (jiǎo) is only a loose sound clue for jī.
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,他非常激动。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā fēicháng jīdòng.
example.english: Hearing this news, he became very worked up.
example.fact: 激动 covers a broader emotional range than English “excited” — it can describe the rush of good news, a surge of anger, or being choked up and moved to tears, unified by the sense of being emotionally stirred up rather than a specifically happy thrill, which is closer to what English speakers mean by “excited.”

examples.pinyin: Bié jīdòng, mànmàn shuō.
examples.english: Don't get excited, speak slowly.

examples.hanzi: 看到老朋友，他激动得说不出话。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào lǎo péngyou, tā jīdòng de shuō bu chū huà.
examples.english: Seeing his old friend, he was too moved to speak.
